resources.string: Guided eye screening — structured like a clinic visit

This app walks you through the same broad sequence many eye clinics use for a basic screening: history, room setup, distance vision each eye, near vision, then a couple of simple supplemental checks. It does not diagnose disease and is not equivalent to a slit-lamp or dilated exam.
In clinic, charts are printed at regulated sizes. Here, match a standard credit card (85.6 mm wide) to the on-screen bar so letter height is in the right ballpark for your phone — still approximate.
Reference width: %1$.1f mm (ISO ID-1 / credit card)
Answer as you would in triage: what you notice day to day. This guides which parts of the self-test to emphasise — it is not a diagnosis.
History complete. Continue to the illustrative blur reference, then the on-screen examination.
Compared with how you expect to see, is it harder for you to see things that are far away, things up close, both, or neither?
Far away (e.g. signs, TV across the room)
Do distant objects or road signs look blurred compared to how you expect?
Do you struggle with small print, phone text, or reading at your usual distance?
Do you get eye strain or frontal headaches with prolonged screen or reading work?
Do you notice glare, halos, or extra difficulty driving at night?
Distance VA — OD (right eye), fellow eye covered
Distance VA — OS (left eye), fellow eye covered
Near vision (both eyes, habitual reading distance)
Some lanes use a mirror or half-silvered chart so you still see the room. Here, an optional live rear-camera preview sits behind the letters — CameraX preview only, not spatial AR tracking.
Camera permission is needed for the live background.

• Use your usual distance glasses or contact lenses if you wear them for driving or TV (unless your clinician told you otherwise).
• Stand about 3 metres from the screen; use a tape measure if unsure.
• Fully cover the eye not being tested — no peeking around the occluder.
• Use bright, even room lighting; avoid glare on the screen.
• Stop if you have sudden vision loss, eye pain, or new flashes/floaters — seek urgent care instead of continuing.

This app provides self-guided wellness screening and education only. It is not a medical device, does not replace a comprehensive eye examination by a licensed professional, and cannot detect all eye disease. Results depend on your device, technique, and environment. Seek urgent in-person care for sudden vision loss, pain, chemical injury, or new flashes and floaters.

Clinic standard: distance visual acuity is tested at a fixed distance (often 4 or 6 m). This app uses ~3 m — stand that far, cover the fellow eye fully, and read the smallest row you can without guessing. Labels are approximate on a phone.
As in clinic: “I will test the right eye first. Keep your glasses on if you use them for distance. Cover the left eye fully. Tell me the letters on the smallest row you can read, left to right.”
“Now the left eye. Keep the right eye fully covered. Same task — smallest clear row, left to right.”
As in clinic near-card testing: “Hold this at your usual reading distance. With both eyes open, pick the smallest print size that is still comfortable.”
Some practices show a radial pattern: “Without squinting, do all lines look equally dark and sharp, or are some segments bolder?”
Simple contrast task: “Which side looks darker and clearer?” There is no single ‘right’ answer for eye health — we only compare your ability to judge contrast today.
Smallest row attempted (approximate label, phone screening): %1$s
Patient response — letters read (same order as chart)
Enter each letter in order, as you would call them aloud to an examiner.
Hold the device at your habitual reading distance (about 35–40 cm). Choose the smallest option you can read comfortably with both eyes — as you would for a near-vision card.
Typical app text or newspaper body.
Look with both eyes at comfortable reading distance. Do all spokes appear equally sharp, or do some look darker or smeared?
Some lines look bolder or smeared
Which panel shows the letter with better contrast?
Adequate, even lighting for this room
I am at ~3 m from the screen (testing distance)
Plays the same instructions and letter row you would hear from staff in a low-vision lane. Uses on-device text-to-speech only.

Optional AI: in debug, set VISIONASSIST_OPENAI_KEY in local.properties for direct OpenAI tips. For release, set proxy_base_url in assets/app_config.json (or host /app-config) so tips go through your backend — never ship API keys in an APK.
AI uses the network. Do not type private health information you would not put on a third-party service.

Illustrative spherical-equivalent feel range: about −%1$.2f to −%2$.2f D (screening only).
This is not autorefraction, retinoscopy, or a phoropter measurement. It cannot replace an in-person refraction or health assessment.

These images apply digital blur only. They do not reproduce real defocus for your exact eye, distance, or screen. Pick the row that feels closest to how uncorrected vision looks to you — this is not a measurement of refractive error.
On this Android version, blur is approximated without full optical blur; use a device with Android 12+ for stronger previews.
